Monitoring Surface Water Chemistry Surface water chemistry is a direct indicator of the effects of acid rain on water bodies. Networks that monitor surface water chemistry over long time periods provide valuable information on aquatic ecosystem health and how water bodies respond to changes in acid-causing emissions. EPA oversees the Long-Term Monitoring (LTM) program, which tracks changes in surface water chemistry in response to changing air pollution and acid deposition. The goal of this long-term program is to track whether the Clean Air Act Amendments (CAAA) ( Plain English Guide to the Clean Air Act ) have been effective in reducing the acidity of surface waters in New England, the Northern Adirondack Mountains, Appalachian Plateau, and the Central Appalachians and advance the science of air pollution impacts on water resources. What are Acidified Surface Waters? Acid precipitation (commonly known as acid rain) primarily affects sensitive bodies of water, which are located in watersheds whose soils have a limited ability to neutralize acidic compounds (called “buffering capacity”). Its Smallest Room Says a Lot About the Thought That Went Into Designing the Space Skip to main content Travel | September 14, 2026 Montana Built a $107 Million Museum. Its Smallest Room Says a Lot About the Thought That Went Into Designing the Space The Montana Heritage Center in Helena has a smudge room. It is open to the public and teaches non-Native visitors why a room dedicated to the burning of cleansing materials, a practice of many Indigenous cultures, is needed The center opened in December 2025. Sarah Bolt/Tempest Technologies The center opened in December 2025. Sarah Bolt/Tempest Technologies You can take a few different paths upon entering the new Montana Heritage Center in Helena. Go left, and explore the life and works of prolific “cowboy artist” Charles M. Russell , creator of more than 2,000 paintings and sculptures of the American West in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Straight ahead are views of the State Capitol. But before any of that, I’d urge you toward the right, to a small plaque marking a windowless room. This room—the smallest in the museum—might be the most important one in the whole place. The plaque marks the smudge room. SERFOR Authorities in Peru say they have foiled a plot to smuggle more than 3,000 tarantulas—including species not yet described in scientific publications—out of the country. After receiving an anonymous tip , officials intercepted three travelers—two German citizens and one Polish citizen—at Jorge Chávez International Airport in Lima as they were checking in at the boarding area. When they searched the travelers’ luggage, they found thousands of eggs, hatchlings and adult spiders hidden in socks, according to a November 4 statement from the National Forest and Wildlife Service of Peru (SERFOR). “We noticed that some of them were moving,” Cora Suárez , a SERFOR forest and wildlife control technician who works at the airport, tells the Agence France-Presse . “There were small ones and large ones.” Workers used slender wooden sticks to gently brush the spiders into clear plastic containers. Once officials are done investigating them, the tarantulas will be taken to an authorized breeding center. Authorities are still trying to identify all the species. pages.description: The International Weightlifting Federation becomes the first Olympic federation to choose Russia to host a world championships since its invasion of Ukraine.
pages.text: Moscow to host 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Weightlifting was first included as an Olympic sport in the 1896 Games in Athens By Craig Nelson BBC Sport Journalist Published 25 October 2026 Updated 27 October 2026 Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in 2022. The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) announced its decision on Sunday, four months after confirming Russian athletes would again be eligible to compete in its events. In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifted a suspension on the Russian Olympic Committee. That suspension had been imposed following the country's invasion of Ukraine. The IOC's subsequent decision potentially opened the way for Russian athletes to compete for their country at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles. This wilderness encompasses an eight-mile-long stretch of the central (and highest) portion of the Black Mountains. Nutt Mountain, at 5,216 feet, presides over a colorful and wild terrain. Along the main ridgeline, prominent mesas have been cut into a series of steep maze-like canyons. Outward from the main ridgeline, numerous huge volcanic plugs ring the entire wilderness. This wilderness is home to desert bighorn sheep. Scattered springs sustain small oases of large cottonwoods, willows, and oaks. Hiking, camping, hunting, photography, and rock scrambling opportunities are varied and challenging. The Clean Air Act identifies two types of national ambient air quality standards. Primary standards provide public health protection, including protecting the health of "sensitive" populations such as asthmatics, children, and the elderly. Secondary standards provide public welfare protection, including protection against decreased visibility and damage to animals, crops, vegetation, and buildings. Together with a blockbuster October study, a new throat bone analysis delivers a “one-two punch” to the 40-year debate over whether Nanotyrannus lancensis was a distinct species. Nanotyrannus lancensis, which recent findings suggest was a distinct dinosaur and not a young Tyrannosaurus rex , was a small-sized Late Cretaceous predator that may have competed with juvenile T.rex for food. Andrey Atuchin, Cleveland Museum of Natural History By Riley Black Published December 4, 2025 Nipping at the heels of a landmark study from October that crowned the short king Nanotyrannus as a legitimate dinosaur, a second team of paleontologists has independently reached the same conclusion: the tiny carnivore was no teen Tyrannosaurus rex but its own distinct species. The new research, published Thursday in Science , comes from an analysis of a small throat bone of the very specimen that set off the decades-old debate. By studying the microscopic details of a peculiar part of the hyoid, called the ceratobranchial, which change with age and comparing it with bones from other animals, such as ostriches, alligators, T. rex , and Allosaurus , the researchers could estimate how mature it was.
